newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares inch up, seen falling on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares inch up, seen falling on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares inched up in stable turnover on Friday but analysts said the supply at order balancing after price fixing and falls in continuous trade could result with a fall at least on Monday.
"We have had strong supply so the market could fall quite significantly on Monday," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment Polska.

The main market's WIG index rose 55.9 points, or 0.3 percent, to 16,424.2, and turnover was stable at 176.3 million zlotys ($55 million) on all three markets as 57 issues rose, 17 fell and 24 were flat.
Analysts said the market could then drift sideways or fall slightly amid forthcoming large privatisations which could draw capital from the bourse.
Analysts said the late May sale of Poland's largest commercial bank, Bank Handlowy SA, was likely to dampen buying of listed shares.
They said the privatisation of copper concern KGHM Polska Miedz, seen taking place in June, could further hurt listed share prices.

Most stocks fell in the continuous trade system, where turnover amounted to 18.1 million zlotys ($5.8 million) and the WIG 20 index closed at 1,592.7 points, 1.7 percent lower than at the regular session.
